# All blobs below are extracted from malbec, build fingerprint:
# Lenovo/TB390FU/TB390FU:16/BQ2A.250610.001-BP2A.250605.031.A3/ZUI_18.0.10.335_260618_ROW:user/release-keys
#
# Generated by work/scripts/12-gen-proprietary-files.py against the
# unpacked factory image.
#
# ★ THE 32 ENTRIES WITH `|<sha1>|<sha1>` ARE HASH-PINNED, AND THAT IS THE ONLY
#   THING STANDING BETWEEN A VENDOR UPDATE AND A SILENTLY HALF-PATCHED BLOB.
#
# Those 32 are exactly the ones extract-files.py rewrites (`blob_fixups`), and
# the two hashes are the file's sha1 BEFORE and AFTER its fixups
# (extract_utils/module.py:939,968 — `file_path_sha1`, not sha256).
#
# The problem this solves: extract-utils compares one hash across a file's WHOLE
# fixup chain (module.py:846-859) and warns only if nothing changed at all. Four
# of these files carry two or three separate `regex_replace`/`replace_needed`
# steps, so one step going dead on the next ZUI drop leaves the other steps
# still changing the file, still changing the hash, and prints nothing.
#
# It matters most for the one fixup in the set that fails OPEN rather than
# closed. Every other `replace_needed` here rewrites a soname to the only
# version installed (display.config→V12, graphics.allocator→V2,
# graphics.common→V7, libtensorflowlite_c→_c_vendor), so losing it leaves an
# unresolvable NEEDED and either the build or 33-blob-linkcheck.py stops. But
# libtinyxml2.so AND libtinyxml2_1.so are both installed, and the composer that
# needs the rewrite also carries ;DISABLE_DEPS — so losing THAT one links
# cleanly, checks green, and SIGILLs on every boot (the 104-byte
# tinyxml2::XMLDocument growth; see the fixup's own comment).
#
# What a pin does: extraction stops with a hash mismatch instead of shipping the
# wrong bytes. That is deliberately a hard failure on the day a legitimate ZUI
# update lands — the cost is re-pinning 32 lines by hand, which is exactly when
# each fixup needs re-reading anyway. Owner decision, session 23.
#
# To re-pin after a vendor update: extract normally, confirm each fixup still
# does what its comment says, then recompute both hashes (the pre-hash is the
# sha1 of the file as it comes out of the factory image, the post-hash is the
# sha1 of the file that lands in vendor/lenovo/malbec/proprietary/).
#
# ⚠️ Every one was verified to have pre != post when the pins were written, i.e.
# all 32 fixups are live today. The count has moved three times — 26 -> 31 -> 32
# (session 25 added media_profiles_tuna_v0.xml) — so treat the number in this
# header as a claim to re-derive, not a fact: `grep -cE '\|[0-9a-f]{40}\|' `
# against the number of blob_fixups keys in extract-files.py. (It said 26 for a
# session; five
# targets carried no pin at all, and they were exactly the fail-open ones --
# work/OPEN-ISSUES.md #56.) A pin where the two hashes are
# equal means the fixup has already died.
#
# Not listed, because the build produces them and a second copy here would
# race the generated one for the same install path:
#   vendor/build.prop, vendor/rfs/**, vendor/etc/{passwd,group},
#   vendor/etc/fs_config_*, vendor/etc/NOTICE.xml.gz,
#   vendor/etc/aconfig_flags.pb (build/make/core/packaging/flags.mk:80),
#   vendor/etc/linker.config.pb (build/make/core/Makefile:4074),
#   vendor/etc/selinux/** (comes from BOARD_VENDOR_SEPOLICY_DIRS),
#   vendor/etc/vintf/compatibility_matrix.xml (DEVICE_MATRIX_FILE) and
#   vendor/etc/vintf/manifest_{kera,sun,tuna}.xml (DEVICE_MANIFEST_FILE ships
#   the tuna one).
#
#   ⚠️ This used to say "the tuna one, which is the SoC this device actually
#   is". That reason was wrong, even though the choice is right. The SoC name
#   here is `sun` (ro.board.platform=sun, ro.soc.model=SM8735P). What actually
#   selects the file is the *vendor SKU*: libvintf picks
#   manifest_<ro.boot.product.vendor.sku>.xml (system/libvintf/VintfObject.cpp,
#   getDeviceHalManifest -> manifest_{sku}.xml, falling back to manifest.xml
#   only on NAME_NOT_FOUND), and this unit reports
#   ro.boot.product.vendor.sku=tuna (checked on the running device). That is
#   also why the 17 StrongBox/SPU entries only present in manifest_sun.xml are
#   correctly absent: they are never loaded on this SKU.
#
# Not listed either: vendor/overlay/** and vendor/etc/assets/** (the 670 MB
# PC Engine container images). The overlays are deliberate, not a tooling
# limitation: RROs belong in the device tree as source (overlay/*Malbec), which
# is what an upstreamable tree does and what onyx does.
#
# system_ext and product carry only the QTI system-side extensions that onyx
# also ships, minus everything cellular — this is a Wi-Fi-only tablet with no
# modem, so the qcril/IMS stack would only retry and log.
#
# ⚠️ vendor/lib64/libtinyxml2.so is DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and the reason is the
# single most important thing on this list. Do not "fix" it by adding it back.
#
# AOSP e26130265cbfe70dd26a22648b1c719406ce2c9e "Upgrade tinyxml2 to 11.0.0"
# turned DynArray's and MemPoolT's `int` members into `size_t`, growing
# sizeof(tinyxml2::XMLDocument) from 776 (0x308) to 880 (0x370). Sixteen blobs
# here link libtinyxml2.so and SEVEN construct an XMLDocument by value, so each
# construction overruns its slot by 104 bytes:
#
#   libpowercore.so          two embedded at this+0x128 / this+0x438, stride 0x310
#   libaudioeffecthal.qti.so memsets exactly 0x308 of stack, constructs there
#   libcamxcoreutils.so      \
#   libcamxods.so             |  not yet triggered -- these fire on first
#   libquasar.so              |  camera open / effect load
#   libapengine.so            |
#   liblearningmodule.so     /
#
# The exported symbol sets of the factory and tree builds are IDENTICAL
# (231 = 231, `diff` of the sorted name lists is empty), because everything that
# moved is private. check_elf_file, 33-blob-linkcheck.py and every other
# symbol-based gate is structurally blind to this class of break.
#
# We cannot ship the factory copy. Android 16 closes all three routes, each
# measured, not assumed:
#
#   1. plain blob entry -> Soong rejects it outright.
#      external/tinyxml2/Android.bp:36 is a plain cc_library with
#      vendor_available, so its partition is `system` even for the vendor
#      variant, and build/soong/android/prebuilt.go:508-517 makes changing
#      partition a hard invariant with its own regression test
#      (prebuilt_test.go:443):
#        "partition is different: system(libtinyxml2) != vendor(prebuilt_libtinyxml2)"
#
#   2. ;MAKE_COPY_RULE_ONLY (a PRODUCT_COPY_FILES rule) -> blocked by the
#      check-non-elf-file-timestamps rule:
#        "found ELF prebuilt in PRODUCT_COPY_FILES, use cc_prebuilt_binary /
#         cc_prebuilt_library_shared instead."
#
#   3. ;MODULE_SUFFIX=_vendor (a differently named prebuilt whose stem still
#      lands on the contested path) -> blocked by the Soong filesystem creator:
#        build/soong/fsgen/Android.bp:41 module "custom_malbec_generated_vendor_image":
#        "packaging conflict at lib64/libtinyxml2.so"
#      Note this one is NEW in Android 16 and it means the "blob wins a
#      contested path" mechanisms in work/analysis/BLOB-CRITERION.md no longer
#      work for anything that lands in a Soong-generated filesystem image.
#      BUILD_BROKEN_DUP_RULES is a kati-level flag and does not apply here.
#
# So the fix is on the consumer side instead: poweropt-service is dropped (it is
# Qualcomm's power-tuning daemon, not needed to boot) and libaudioeffecthal.qti
# is built from source, where it is compiled against the v11 header and reserves
# the right 880 bytes. The five CamX/effects libraries above are still armed;
# see work/analysis/OPEN-ISSUES.md for the exposure and the options.

# APEX
vendor/apex/com.google.android.widevine.nonupdatable.apex

# Apps
vendor/app/CACertService/CACertService.apk
vendor/app/TimeService/TimeService.apk
vendor/app/TrustZoneAccessService/TrustZoneAccessService.apk
vendor/app/com.qualcomm.qti.gpudrivers.sun.api35/com.qualcomm.qti.gpudrivers.sun.api35.apk;PRESIGNED
vendor/priv-app/pasrservice/pasrservice.apk

# ⚠️ The whole QVR / SXR / xrcomm (Qualcomm XR) stack is DELIBERATELY ABSENT.
# 58 entries were removed in session 12. Do not re-extract them.
#
# Two independent reasons:
#
#   1. It is an active memory-corruption hazard on Android 16.
#      frameworks/native df868baf2a "Introduce a dependency monitor for fences"
#      added mDependencyMonitor to android::GraphicBuffer, taking it from 256 to
#      3376 bytes (A16 DWARF DW_AT_byte_size = 0x0d30, verified against
#      out/.../symbols/system/lib64/libui.so). Exactly three shipped blobs import
#      GraphicBuffer's constructors -- criterion `llvm-nm -D -u | grep
#      _ZN7android13GraphicBufferC[123]E`, swept over every blob in the image:
#
#        vendor/lib64/libqvrservice.so           (4 operator new(256) sites)
#        vendor/lib64/libsxrservice.so           (14)
#        vendor/lib64/libxrcommnetworkservice.so (1)
#
#      Each one allocates 256 bytes and then runs the A16 constructor, which
#      writes out to 0xd30 -- a 3120-byte heap overflow per buffer. These are not
#      dormant: the s12 boot log has "sxrservice: QVRSplitService instantiated"
#      and "sxrservice: started". libui cannot be pinned to A15 (the whole
#      graphics stack sits on it) and the XR blobs have no source, so removal is
#      the only correct fix. Same class as the tinyxml2 break in extract-files.py,
#      and equally invisible to every symbol-based gate -- GraphicBuffer's
#      exported symbol set did not change at all.
#
#   2. This is a tablet. There is no headset, no 6DoF tracking rig and no XR
#      display. The only qvr config sets shipped are for other reference boards
#      (mtpkailua = soc 519, mtplanai = soc 557); this unit is soc 694, and the
#      log shows exactly that: "QVRServiceConfiguration: opendir failed for
#      /vendor/etc/qvr/cfg/694/0/65536/".
#
# Verified safe before removing: no non-XR file anywhere in the built image has
# any of the 30 XR .so files in its DT_NEEDED, and no non-XR config names one.
#
# Removing the stack also deletes vendor/bin/init.qvrd.usb_mtu_set.sh, which was
# the single shipped vendor service with no SELinux exec label.

# ⚠️ Four more entries are deliberately absent, all "declared but not
# implemented" dead weight (removed in session 12):
#
#   vendor/etc/vintf/manifest/vendor.qti.hardware.power.powermodule.xml
#   vendor/lib64/vendor.qti.hardware.power.powermodule-V1-ndk.so
#   vendor/lib64/libpowercallback.so
#     Session 11 dropped vendor/bin/poweropt-service (its libpowercore.so
#     embeds a tinyxml2::XMLDocument by value and SIGSEGV'd), but left the VINTF
#     fragment behind. The device was therefore ADVERTISING
#     vendor.qti.hardware.power.powermodule.IPowerModule/default with nothing
#     implementing it -- confirmed present in the built image with
#     `debugfs -R "ls -l /etc/vintf/manifest" vendor.img` (313 bytes). Nothing
#     blocks on it today (libpowercallback.so has zero consumers anywhere in the
#     image, checked by DT_NEEDED sweep) but a false declaration is a trap.
#
#   vendor/bin/hw/android.hardware.keymaster@4.0-service-qti
#     No .rc anywhere and no VINTF declaration -- on the factory image either.
#     It has never been started on this device. Pure dead weight.

# ⚠️ vendor/etc/**/sku_kera/** and vendor/etc/**/sku_sun/** (and their _qssi
# variants) are DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Removed in session 12.
#
# The factory vendor image is shared across three SoCs and ships all three SKU
# trees. This unit is `tuna` and can never read the other two. Proven twice, from
# both ends:
#
#   · the consumers build the path from a property, not from a build-time choice:
#       strings libar-pal.so            -> "ro.boot.product.vendor.sku", "/vendor/etc/audio/sku_"
#       strings libaudiocorehal.qti.so  -> same
#     and the device reports ro.boot.product.vendor.sku=tuna.
#   · the running device only ever opened the tuna copies -- from the s12 boot
#     log, /vendor/etc/audio/sku_tuna/{mixer_paths_tuna_qrd,audio_effects_config,
#     resourcemanager_tuna_qrd,mcs_defs_tuna_qrd}.xml and
#     /vendor/etc/permissions/sku_tuna/*.xml, with zero hits for kera or sun.
#
# Same reasoning already applies to the VINTF manifests: libvintf picks
# manifest_<ro.boot.product.vendor.sku>.xml, which is why only manifest_tuna.xml
# is shipped (see the note at the top of this file).
#
# ⚠️ Do NOT generalise this to "delete anything with another SoC's name in it"
# without first finding what selects the file. sku_tuna is chosen by a property
# here; elsewhere the selector may be a build variable or a DT lookup.

# ⚠️ 157 more entries are deliberately absent, removed in session 14. Each was
# re-verified three ways before deletion, because the previous rounds were burned
# by exactly the checks that get skipped: a DT_NEEDED index over all 3043 ELFs in
# the built image, a raw byte-string scan of the whole image tree for the
# basename AND for the soname with `.so` stripped (this is what finds a dlopen /
# System.loadLibrary that the link graph cannot show — libsdmextension.so was
# missed that way once), and a service/reference sweep over all 222 shipped .rc
# files. Evidence per line is in work/analysis/S14-cleanup.md.
#
#   64  Telephony / RIL / IMS / UIM / LPA / CNE interface libraries, plus
#       vendor/bin/nicmd + nicmd.rc + libnicm_modemproxy.so. ro.baseband=apq,
#       no modem, zero radio HALs. Session 13 removed the implementations and
#       left the interface libraries; the cluster is closed — every one of them
#       has either no DT_NEEDED consumer at all or only consumers inside the
#       set. nicmd is Qualcomm's Network Interface Configuration Manager
#       (rmnet/cellular data plumbing): it was `class main`, no `disabled`,
#       running as root on every boot, and it is the ONLY consumer of
#       libnicm_modemproxy.so. The other libnicm* libraries stay — libnicm.so
#       is still pulled in by libdsi_netctrl.so / libnicm_dsi.so / libnicm_vh.so.
#
#   54  vendor/etc/sensors/config/{eliza,pakala}_*.json — two other boards'
#       sensor registries. This board is the `bonito_` family: dumpsys
#       sensorservice on the running unit reports exactly lsm6dsv (STMicro),
#       gs6155 (goodix), aw963xx0 (awinic SAR) and bu52053nvx (ROHM hall), and
#       only bonito_* has a config for the first three. eliza/pakala carry
#       lsm6dso, icm4x6xx, mmc56x3x, tmd3765/tmd2755, sx932x, sht4x, lps22df —
#       none of which the device has ever registered.
#       json.lst still names them, and that is fine: the registry loader
#       tolerates missing entries. Stock's OWN json.lst names 4 files that do
#       not exist in stock's own config dir (qsh_camera_imx688_4.json,
#       sns_amd_sw_disabled.json, sns_presence_detect.json,
#       sns_tilt_sw_disabled.json) and stock's sensors work.
#
#   14  The poweropt cluster: six /vendor/etc/pwr/*.xml and seven .so
#       (libpowercore + lib{aod,camera,game,offscreen,psm,video}optfeature +
#       libstandbyfeature). Session 11 already dropped its only loader,
#       vendor/bin/poweropt-service — that binary is the sole DT_NEEDED consumer
#       of libpowercore.so in the FACTORY image, and nothing in ours consumes any
#       of the seven. PowerFeatureConfig.xml is named by libpowercore.so and by
#       nothing else. This also retires one of the seven live tinyxml2 hazards
#       listed above for free.
#       ⚠️ libstandbyfeature.so is in this list even though it is not an
#       "optfeature": it DT_NEEDEDs libpowercore.so, so removing libpowercore
#       without it would leave a dangling dependency and 33-blob-linkcheck.py
#       would go red.
#
#   10  Sample / test artefacts with 0 .rc stanzas and 0 references anywhere:
#       drm_sample_app, TrustedUISampleTAClient, smcinvoke_{example,skeleton,
#       skeleton_cpp}, GPTEE_Sample_client, qmi_test_mt_client_init_instance,
#       libvpptestutils.so, and vendor/etc/perf/test{common,target}resourceconfigs.xml
#       (libqti-perfd.so names commonresourceconfigs.xml and
#       targetresourceconfigs.xml, never the test* pair).
#       ⚠️ vendor/lib64/libtestutils.so is NOT one of these — despite the name it
#       is a DT_NEEDED of libsdmextension.so. vendor/bin/mm-audio-ftm is not
#       either; it has one .rc reference and two binary references.
#
#    8  Foreign camera sensors. The four modules on this board are named in the
#       sensormodule/tuned pairs below: malbec_{ofilm_ov08f10,qtech_ov13b10,
#       sunwin_gc08a8,txd_ov13b10}. Removed: the IMX688 and OV32C4C qsh JSONs and
#       .pb tuning blobs (the three .pb files in vendor/lib64/camera were the
#       ONLY .pb files there — this board ships none), and
#       com.qti.eeprom.gt24p128e2csli_s5kjn1.so (Samsung S5KJN1; none of the four
#       sensormodule .bin files names gt24p128e2csli or s5kjn1 — they name
#       malbec_ov13b10_eeprom and malbec_txd_ov13b10_eeprom).
#
#    2  Fingerprint residue on a device with no fingerprint sensor:
#       vendor.qti.hardware.fingerprint@1.0.so (0 consumers) and
#       vendor/etc/permissions/qti_fingerprint_interface.xml, which declared a
#       shared library at /system/framework/vendor.qti.hardware.fingerprint-V1-java.jar
#       — a jar this build does not contain.
#
#    2  XR eye-tracking stubs the session-12 XR purge missed:
#       vendor/lib/rfsa/adsp/libeye_tracking_dsp_sample_skel.so and
#       vendor/lib64/libeye_tracking_dsp_sample_stub.so. 0 consumers each; a
#       headset feature, on a tablet, and by name a *sample*.
#
#    2  GNSS residue: libslimclient.so (0 consumers; slim_daemon went in s13) and
#       vendor/etc/sap.conf (SLIM/SAP sensor-assisted positioning). sap.conf is
#       named only by libgps.utils.so, in a table of eleven /vendor/etc/*.conf
#       paths of which FOUR are already absent from this image (gps.conf,
#       izat.conf, xtwifi.conf, gnss_antenna_info.conf) while the LOWI Wi-Fi
#       location stack keeps working — loc_read_conf falls back to defaults.
#
#    1  vendor/etc/permissions/noRil/apq_excluded_telephony_features.xml. It is
#       inert where it sits: SystemConfig.readPermissions(parser, dir, flags)
#       does `for (File f : libraryDir.listFiles()) if (!f.isFile()) continue;`
#       (frameworks/base/.../SystemConfig.java:797+), and the only subdirectories
#       it descends into are sku_$(ro.boot.product.vendor.sku) and
#       sku_$(ro.boot.product.hardware.sku). `noRil` is neither, so its twelve
#       <unavailable-feature android.hardware.telephony*> lines were never read.
#       Removing it changes nothing at runtime: nothing in this image declares
#       any android.hardware.telephony feature in the first place (the only other
#       hit for that string is two comment lines in handheld_core_hardware.xml).
#
# ⚠️ Two entries the session-14 audit proposed and this list DELIBERATELY KEEPS:
#
#   vendor/etc/media_codecs_google_telephony.xml
#     It has two live consumers, both of them files we also ship:
#     vendor/etc/media_codecs.xml:113 and vendor/etc/media_codecs_tuna_v0.xml:110
#     each carry <Include href="media_codecs_google_telephony.xml" />. The parse
#     failure would be benign (MediaCodecsXmlParser.cpp:528-533 sets
#     NAME_NOT_FOUND, and combineStatus() at :113-118 explicitly folds
#     NAME_NOT_FOUND into OK), but deleting the target of an <Include> we ship
#     without also patching the two includes is half a change for 900 bytes.
#
#   vendor/lib64/camera/bitmlconfig_sm7550.bin
#     It names another SoC, but the retained and heavily consumed
#     vendor/lib64/libbitmlenginev2.so contains the literal string
#     "bitmlconfig_sm7550.bin" next to "bitmlconfig.bin", and picks between them
#     through SocUtils::GetSocId() / OverrideSocId. Which SoC ids map to which
#     file is inside generated code (g_bitml/camxbitmlconfig.cpp) that we cannot
#     read. 620 bytes is not worth guessing at the camera. See the warning above
#     about "another SoC's name in it".

# ★ BOTH panel suppliers. This panel is dual sourced -- BOE nt36536e and
# CSOT nt36536 -- and nvt_touch.ko builds the firmware filename from the
# panel name it reads at probe. Our own boot log, on a CSOT unit:
#     [NVT-ts] nvt_update_tp_module_info: fw name = csot_novatek_ts_fw.bin
# so on a BOE unit it asks for boe_novatek_ts_fw.bin instead. Session 15
# dropped the BOE pair as "another panel"; it is not another panel, it is
# the same panel from the other supplier, and without these two files a BOE
# unit gets no touch firmware update at all. 0.5 MB for a whole hardware
# variant of this exact model.

# Permissions
#
# ⚠️ Only the three Qualcomm-owned files are left here. The other 34 —
# handheld_core_hardware.xml, every android.hardware.*/android.software.* feature
# XML, and the six sensor files stock hid under sku_tuna/ — moved to
# PRODUCT_COPY_FILES in device.mk in session 25 (work/OPEN-ISSUES.md #64).
#
# The reason is the failure mode, not tidiness. A feature XML has no build-time
# edge of any kind: nothing links it, no check_elf_file inspects it, no VINTF
# check reads it. A re-extraction that dropped handheld_core_hardware.xml would
# produce a GREEN build of a tablet with no launcher, no input method and no lock
# screen, because that one file declares android.software.home_screen,
# android.software.input_methods and android.software.secure_lock_screen. 34 of
# the 36 were verified byte-identical to files already in this checkout, so
# nothing was lost by sourcing them upstream; the two that were not have copies in
# configs/permissions/ with their derivations written down.
#
# ⚠️ Do NOT re-add the moved lines on the next ZUI drop. If a future drop changes
# one of them, the acceptance gate is what should tell you: 24-blob-reconcile.py
# compares stock's partition against ours by path, and these paths still ship.

vendor/etc/permissions/vendor.qti.dcf.xml
vendor/etc/permissions/vendor.qti.qva.xml

# Battery

# ⚠️ THE bm5a* FILES BELOW ARE NOT BATTERY ANYTHING. They inherited this section
# header by position and it has been misleading ever since — "bm" is not
# "battery model". Identified in session 22 by reading one of them:
#
#     min_arch=73; num_hmx=4; hvx_threads=4; vtcm_mb=8; hmx_type=fg;
#     ConvLayer.opt.weights_to_vtcm@Xpb.xpb.  @DmaCheckpointSet  @SyncOp
#
# They are **compiled Qualcomm Hexagon NPU (HTP) neural-network graphs**. The 73
# in the name is the Hexagon architecture and matches `min_arch=73` inside the
# file, which is what settles that the bm5a79* family belongs to a different
# NSP revision and is correctly not extracted.
#
# ★ 51 files x ~5 MB = 211 MB, i.e. ROUGHLY 18 % OF THE VENDOR PARTITION, and
# this tree cannot say what loads them. Measured in session 22:
#
#   · A byte-level scan of every file in every stock partition — vendor, odm,
#     system, product, system_ext — for "bm5a", "s13n", "73v0" and "79v0" finds
#     NOTHING. Every hit is a coincidence inside a mangled C++ or Rust symbol.
#     So the filename is constructed at runtime from pieces, or nothing loads
#     them at all.
#   · On the running device, no process has one open or mapped
#     (/proc/*/maps and /proc/*/fd swept).
#
# Stock ships three families (bm5a73v04, bm5a73v08, bm5a79v08 — 154 files,
# ~640 MB). This tree takes the 51 bm5a73v08.
#
# ★★ SETTLED IN SESSION 24 — the consumer has a name, and v08 is right for this
# SoC. The loader is /vendor/lib64/libbitmlenginev2.so, Qualcomm's CamX "BITML
# Engine V2", and the reason no byte scan could ever find these filenames is that
# it never contains one: CamX::BITMLNetwork::setNetworkConfig() builds the path
# by appending seven short fragments —
#
#     "/vendor/lib64/" + "bm5" + <arch> + <vtcm> + "s13" + "n" + <2-digit id> + ".bin"
#
# — then fopen()s it and hands the buffer to bitml_nsp_v2_domains_deserialize()
# over FastRPC to the CDSP.
#
# ✔ Confirmed without disassembly, which is what makes it checkable here:
# `strings -n 3` on that library yields each of `bm5`, `a68`, `a73`, `a75`,
# `a79`, `v04`, `v08`, `s13`, `.bin` and `/vendor/lib64/` EXACTLY ONCE, as
# standalone strings. Ten single-use fragments is the append construction made
# visible.
#
# Selection is by soc_id (SocUtils::GetSocId(), overridable by an `OverrideSocId`
# line in camxoverridesettings.txt, which our shipped copy does not have):
# 655/694 -> a73 + v08. This unit reads 694 / TUNAP
# (`cat /sys/devices/soc0/soc_id /sys/devices/soc0/machine`). `v04`/`v08` are
# literally vtcm_mb=4 / vtcm_mb=8, matching the blobs' own metadata.
#
# ★ So v08 is not a coin toss and it is not per-unit: soc_id is fixed for the
# whole TB390FU model, so unlike the media_tuna_v1 / camera-tuning cases there is
# no other unit to insure against. The tree was already coherent with itself
# without knowing why — it ships vendor/lib64/rfs/dsp/libbitml_nsp_73na_skel.so
# and deliberately not the _79na_ skel, which is the DSP side only the a79 blobs
# could use.
#
# ⚠️ Still do NOT also ship v04 or a79: 211 MB and 211 MB respectively, for
# families this SoC's selection chain provably never reaches.
#
# (The 26 missing indices in the n00-n77 range are not gaps —
# getNetworkIDFromName bounds at 77 contiguous IDs and not every network has a
# compiled graph for this arch/vtcm build.) See work/OPEN-ISSUES.md #39/#52.
vendor/lib64/bm5a73v08s13n00.bin
vendor/lib64/bm5a73v08s13n01.bin

# ── Session 20 removed 35 entries; the evidence is in the allowlist ──────────
#
# SOTER (fingerprint-payment attestation on a device with no fingerprint
# sensor), C2PA content credentials (the Java half is ZUI-side), three
# ZUI-app-only JNI libraries, the Wi-Fi Alliance sigma_dut certification
# plumbing, six binaries with no `service` stanza in ANY shipped or factory .rc,
# two debug kernel-tuning scripts, five thermal profiles vendor.thermal.mode can
# never select here, one Hexagon skel whose own dependency is absent from the
# factory package, and libquasar.so.
#
# The per-entry reasoning is in work/analysis/vendor-gap-allowlist.txt under the
# nine `s20-*` categories, which is also what keeps 32-acceptance.py check 2
# honest about them. It is written there rather than here because that file is
# what the check reads: a justification only this file carries is a
# justification the tooling cannot see.
#
# ⚠️ Two of the traps that survived the sweep, recorded so nobody "finishes the
# job" by removing them:
#   * libsoc_helper.so (no `_jni`) is DT_NEEDED by the shipped Bluetooth HAL.
#     Only libsoc_helper_jni.so went.
#   * libjnihelper.so looks dead by soname and is loaded by CACertService.apk as
#     "jnihelper" — System.loadLibrary uses the SHORT name, so a soname search
#     cannot see it.

# Audio
vendor/bin/adsprpcd
vendor/bin/audioadsprpcd
# The Awinic smart-amplifier calibration tool. Not on the playback path — nothing
# starts it, there is no .rc for it, and leaving it out cost nothing at runtime.
# It is here because it is the ONLY working instrument for reading the amplifier
# algorithm's state back out of the DSP, and its absence is what let a wrong
# diagnosis survive seven rounds.
#
# The four sysfs nodes that look like the instrument — algo_state, dsp_re,
# f0_show, cali_re — are compile-time CONSTANTS of this kernel module build.
# aw882xx_dlkm.ko has no apr_/gpr_/afe_/q6 symbol of any kind, its
# aw_read_msg_from_dsp_v_1_0_0_0 has an empty transport hook and zero indirect
# calls, and aw882xx_cali_read_re_from_nvram is a 12-byte `mov w0,wzr; ret`
# stub. They print "read algo run state failed!" and three zeroes in every
# state, on stock ZUI included. The full derivation is in
# work/analysis/OPEN-ISSUES.md §13.
#
# This tool instead goes the way PAL does — aw_ar_dsp_get_miid over tinyalsa
# mixer controls into the SPF graph — so it can actually read the DSP:
#   aw882xx_cali aw882xx_smartpa get_spkr_st    R0/F0 per channel
#   aw882xx_cali aw882xx_smartpa get_re_range   the accepted Re window
#   aw882xx_cali aw882xx_smartpa cali           re-run calibration
# It is also the only way to regenerate /mnt/vendor/persist/factory/audio/
# aw_cali.bin if that per-unit file is ever lost, which no other shipped
# component can do.
vendor/bin/aw882xx_cali
vendor/bin/hw/vendor.qti.media.c2audio@1.0-service

# Display
# ⚠️ The whole SDM cluster below is a BLOB, and reverting that to a source build
# is what cost session 11 an entire round. Read this before "cleaning it up".
#
# The factory SDM is a Lenovo/Motorola private fork. It is not any public CAF
# tag, and the fork is not published:
#
#   nm -D --defined-only work/unpacked/parts/vendor/lib64/libsdmcore.so | c++filt
#     sdm::DisplayBase::SetMotoColor(unsigned, int, snapdragoncolor::MotoColorParams*)
#     sdm::DisplayBase::SetRGBASplit(int)
#     sdm::DPUColorManager::ColorMgrSetMotoColor(...)      libsdmclient: SDMDisplay::*
#     sdm::HWDeviceDRM::SetMotoPAHsic(...)                 libsdmdal:    HWDeviceDRM::*
#   grep -rn "SetMotoColor\|RGBASplit" hardware/qcom-caf/sm8750/display/   ->  0 hits
#
# The fork changed class layout. Measured with llvm-nm -S -D (symbol sizes) and
# the non-virtual thunk offsets, factory vs a source build of the same library:
#
#   sdm::DisplayBase        161 vtable slots   vs 159   (+2: the two Moto methods)
#   sdm::DisplayBuiltIn     208                vs 206
#   sdm::DisplayPluggable   196                vs 194
#   DisplayBase data        +48 bytes  (thunks 12864/12872/12880 vs 12816/12824/12832)
#   control: libsdmclient thunk offsets are IDENTICAL in both, so the measurement
#            detects real differences rather than build noise.
#
# libsdmextension.so (2.3 MB, the SDM resource manager and strategy) is closed
# source and is built from that fork. libsdmcore dlopen()s it -- core_impl.cpp:80,
# name from extension_interface.h:49 -- so it appears in NO DT_NEEDED and no
# link-graph tool can see the coupling. DispLayerStack* is handed straight across
# that boundary (resource_interface.h:75-118, strategy_interface.h:58,72,
# partial_update_interface.h:49), all pure virtual, implemented in the blob.
#
# Building the open half from source against that blob produced 50 tombstones,
# all in sdm::DispLayerStack::Clear(), in three flavours -- 26 "Pointer tag was
# truncated" (free() on a garbage pointer), 23 "ubsan: mul-overflow", 1 "Scudo
# misaligned pointer". Three different aborts in one function is memory
# corruption, not arithmetic. The corrupted field is HWLayersInfo::layer_exts
# (hw_info_types.h:1108) -- and `grep -rn layer_exts` over the entire sm8750
# display tree returns only the declaration. The open source never writes it;
# only the blob does (sdm::ResourceAlloc::HandleExclRect(DispLayerStack*)).
#
# Note what is NOT the reason: sizeof(HWLayersInfo) is 107408 and sizeof(Layer)
# is 6336 on BOTH sides. The structs crossing the boundary did not change size.
# This is a behavioural fork mismatch, not a struct-layout ABI break, and the
# exact instruction where the blob corrupts the vector was never pinned down.
#
# Swapping in only libsdmcore.so does not work either: libsdmclient and libsdmdal
# are forked too, and a source-built libsdmclient makes virtual calls on
# DisplayInterface* against a vtable that has two extra slots. Symbol closure
# resolving is NOT the same as vtable slots lining up.
#
# The factory ROM is the existence proof that this blob set is correct here: its
# fingerprint is TB390FU:16/... -- Android 16 framework over a 202404-frozen
# vendor, exactly the Treble configuration this tree ships. onyx does the same
# (its proprietary-files.txt:2261,2274-2296,2320 take the entire cluster).
#
# device.mk must NOT put any of these back into PRODUCT_PACKAGES.
system_ext/lib64/libwfddisplayconfig.so|6d5ed77a65d765e48a23f3519c6c7a5005945086|0ec23909490dc70c6289a00752fa2c541b664221

vendor/bin/hw/android.hardware.power-service
# ★ The thermal HAL is a BLOB, and it is the one QTI HAL in this tree whose
# source build is provably wrong for this board.
#
# hardware/qcom-caf/thermal is Qualcomm's reference config, keyed on soc_id. For
# 694 (tuna) thermalConfig.cpp:2487-2500 maps TemperatureType::SKIN to thermal
# zone `sys-therm-3`, and Lenovo's board does not populate it. Measured: all 75
# zones enumerated, the only sys-therm-* present are -0 (live) and -2/-4 (both
# read -40960, i.e. open circuit). Stock's own zone dump has the identical set,
# so this is the board, not a kernel difference.
#
# The consequence is not a missing number, it is a missing framework subsystem:
#
#   E ThermalManagerService$ThermalHalWrapper: Couldn't getTemperatureThresholds
#     due to invalid status ... IllegalStateException: ThermalHAL given sensor
#     type not initialized.
#       at ...TemperatureWatcher.getAndUpdateThresholds(:2019)
#
# TemperatureWatcher IS thermal headroom. With no SKIN sensor,
# PowerManager.getThermalHeadroom() has nothing to compute from, skin
# temperature never raises THERMAL_STATUS_*, and
# HardwarePropertiesManager.getDeviceTemperatures(SKIN) returns nothing. Games
# and the camera use all three to slow themselves down before the tablet gets
# uncomfortable to hold. (Hardware protection is unaffected — thermal-engine and
# the kernel cooling devices never went through this HAL.)
#
# The right zone is `quiet-therm`, proven rather than guessed. Stock's dumpsys
# and its sysfs snapshot were taken at the same instant — vbat reads 4.434 /
# 4434 and battery 29.9 / 29900 in the pair — and in that same instant:
#
#     stock dumpsys :  Temperature{mValue=31.328, mType=3, mName=skin}
#     stock sysfs   :  quiet-therm = 31323     <- 5 millidegrees, one sample
#                      sys-therm-0 = 32790
#                      ap-therm    = 33341
#
# So Lenovo's blob has the mapping this board needs and the tree's source build
# cannot get it: hardware/qcom-caf/thermal is upstream, the config is a compiled
# table, and there is no property, file or soong_config hook to override it.
#
# ✔ Proven on the hardware before being written down. Bind-mounted the stock
# blob over ours and restarted vendor.thermal-hal:
#     Temperature{mValue=31.084, mType=3, mName=skin}   (quiet-therm = 31089)
#     the full threshold table prints with NO exception, skin thresholds
#     [-, 48, 49, 50, 60, 61, 90] — identical to tuna_specific's, i.e. the same
#     config with a zone name that exists.
#
# Why the ABI is safe, which is the question this tree always asks of an
# Android-15 blob (libgpu_tonemapper, libaudioeffecthal.qti, vndservicemanager):
# readelf -d gives a NEEDED list byte-identical to our source build, and the C++
# undefined symbols are libc++ (stable ABI) plus four android::base::LogMessage
# entry points plus BnThermal from the FROZEN android.hardware.thermal-V2-ndk —
# the same version our source build links. Not one libutils C++ symbol, so there
# is no AOSP object whose size could have grown underneath it. vndservicemanager
# was the opposite case: it implements a libbinder C++ Bn* whose vtable AOSP
# reorders at will.
#
# ⚠️ The .rc and the VINTF fragment MUST come with it. They reach the image today
# as the source module's init_rc:/vintf_fragments:, and `prefer: true` disables
# that module completely. A binary with no .rc never starts; a service with no
# fragment is never declared. Both halves of OPEN-ISSUES.md #34, in one change.
#
# ⚠️ Acceptance test after the next flash, because a 90-second bind-mount does
# not exercise the callback path: `dumpsys thermalservice` must list
# `mType=3, mName=skin`, and a sustained load must move `Thermal Status` off 0
# without a HAL death.
vendor/bin/hw/android.hardware.thermal-service.qti

vendor/bin/hw/vendor.qti.hardware.perf2-hal-service

# ★ BOTH vidc revisions of the media config, and the _v1 half is insurance for a
# tablet that is not this one.
#
# /vendor/bin/init.qti.media.sh:60-71 picks the suffix at RUNTIME off a silicon
# register, not off the model:
#
#     sku_ver=`cat /sys/devices/platform/soc/aa00000.qcom,vidc/sku_version`
#     if [ $sku_ver -eq 1 ]; then setprop vendor.media.target_variant "_tuna_v1"; fi
#
# This unit reads 0, and `getprop vendor.media.target_variant` confirms `_tuna_v0`
# — so shipping only _v0 works here and would keep working here forever. On a
# TB390FU whose vidc reports 1 it selects `_tuna_v1`, finds nothing, and the media
# framework comes up with no codec list, no performance table and no profiles.
# The device tree cannot know which revision someone else's tablet has.
#
# 95 KB for four files against a whole-subsystem failure that would only ever
# appear on hardware the maintainer does not own. Found by the blob-gap sweep
# (OPEN-ISSUES.md #39); it is the clearest case in that list of a gap that is
# invisible on the bench and fatal in the field.

# System-side QTI
#
# system_ext/lib64/libdiag_system.so is deliberately NOT extracted. It needs
# vendor.qti.diaghal-V1-ndk.so, which exists only in /vendor/lib64 and is out of
# reach of the system_ext linker namespace (Android 16 has no VNDK, so the system
# section sees only /system/lib64 and /system_ext/lib64).
# On stock its consumers are diag_mdlog_system, dpmd, mmi and lib-imsvt.so — the
# diagnostic and IMS components this tree deliberately does not extract. A
# binary-safe scan of this whole image finds zero references. Installing it would
# ship a library guaranteed to fail to resolve.
# ★ The Java half of Miracast. Extracted from /system/framework and installed to
# /system_ext/framework, which is not a tidy-up — it is the path the code in THIS
# tree looks at.
#
# ExtendedRemoteDisplayHelper is the AOSP-side integration point and
# WifiDisplayController:767,775 dispatches through it. It resolves the class two
# ways, in order (ExtendedRemoteDisplayHelper.java:63-79):
#
#     Class.forName("com.qualcomm.wfd.ExtendedRemoteDisplay")        // boot classpath
#     new PathClassLoader("/system_ext/framework/WfdCommon.jar", …)  // fallback
#
# and WFD_COMMON_JAR at :46 is that literal system_ext path. Verified the class
# is actually in the archive rather than assumed from the name: the jar holds one
# classes.dex and Lcom/qualcomm/wfd/ExtendedRemoteDisplay; is in its string pool.
#
# ⚠️ Deliberately NOT ;BOOT_JAR, which is what this line said first. Stock does
# use the boot classpath (system/etc/classpaths/bootclasspath.pb lists
# /system/framework/WfdCommon.jar) and onyx tags the identical file that way, so
# copying either of them looked right. It is the heavier of the two routes here:
# PRODUCT_BOOT_JARS pulls a vendor prebuilt into dexpreopt, the boot image
# profile and derive_classpath's bootclasspath.pb, i.e. into every process on the
# device — to reach a class that one class in system_server loads reflectively
# and that the second route reaches with no platform change at all. The rest of
# the WFD stack already lives in system_ext (wfdservice64, WfdService.apk and
# twenty libwfd*.so), so this puts the jar with its own stack.
#
# The boot-classpath route was checked before being rejected, not assumed to be
# broken: com.qualcomm.wfd IS on the allowlist that would otherwise fail the
# build (build/soong/scripts/check_boot_jars/package_allowed_list.txt, "# QC
# adds"). It would work. It is simply more blast radius than the job needs.
# ★ The boot animation is NOT extracted. It was, up to session 20, and the
# reason it is not any more is a real difference between the two ROMs rather
# than a change of taste.
#
# Under PixelOS there was no choice. That project ships three fixed PORTRAIT
# assets (720/1080/1440) and picks one by TARGET_SCREEN_WIDTH, and BootAnimation
# does NOT scale — playAnimation computes
#
#     animationY = (display.height - animation.height) / 2
#
# and draws at native pixel size (BootAnimation.cpp:1649-1665; ratioW/ratioH are
# display.width/display.initWidth, i.e. 1.0 here). Against this device's 3504x2190
# landscape boot surface the 1080 asset gives animationY = (2190 - 2424) / 2 =
# -117 and clips 13 px off the bottom; the 1440 asset clips 4. Nothing selectable
# fit, so stock's `3504 2190 12` animation was the only one that did.
#
# LineageOS GENERATES the animation at this device's own size instead of picking
# a prebuilt: vendor/lineage/bootanimation/gen-bootanimation.sh:35-52 takes
# IMAGEWIDTH = min(TARGET_SCREEN_HEIGHT, TARGET_SCREEN_WIDTH) = 2190 and emits
# 2190x730 frames with a matching desc.txt. On the landscape boot surface that
# leaves 657 px of margin either side and 730 above and below. The constraint
# that forced the extraction simply does not exist here.
#
# The device owner asked for the LineageOS animation (session 21).
#
# Two consequences worth knowing:
#   · one of the 23 duplicate install targets disappears —
#     product/media/bootanimation.zip no longer has a blob PRODUCT_COPY_FILES
#     competing with vendor/lineage's module. Re-record with
#     `python3 work/scripts/30-dup-installs.py --write`.
#   · TARGET_BOOTANIMATION_HALF_RES is deliberately left at its `false` default
#     (vendor/lineage/config/BoardConfigSoong.mk:26). Half res does not shrink
#     the animation — desc.txt still says 2190x730 — it renders 1095x365 PNGs and
#     lets BootAnimation upscale them 2x, which on a 3.5K panel is visible.
system/framework/WfdCommon.jar:system_ext/framework/WfdCommon.jar

# ★ The two Haptics files, on a tablet with no vibrator motor — added session 25 as
# insurance, not as a feature.
#
# libar-pal.so names exactly four absolute XML paths, and three of them ship:
#   /vendor/etc/card-defs.xml  /vendor/etc/mem_logger_config.xml
#   /vendor/etc/usecaseKvManager.xml  /vendor/etc/Hapticsconfig.xml   <- was missing
#
# It is inert TODAY for a better reason than "there is no motor" (#6's argument,
# which depends on a hardware claim): resourcemanager_tuna_qrd.xml:54 says
# `<param key="haptics_through_wsa" value="false"/>`, ResourceManager.cpp:579
# initialises the flag false and only :9396 sets it from that key, and the call at
# :1063-1070 is inside `if (isHapticsthroughWSA)`. So the file is never opened.
#
# ⚠️ Why it ships anyway. AudioHapticsInterface.cpp:65-73 does not degrade on a
# parse failure — it `throw std::runtime_error("error in haptics xml parsing")`,
# and ResourceManager's constructor throws again on a non-zero return. That is an
# exception out of the constructor of the object audiohalservice.qti is built
# around: **no audio at all, plus a respawn loop**, with a log line pointing at
# haptics on a device with no vibrator. The whole distance between inert and that
# is one attribute in a 94 KB vendor file nobody diffs. 25.8 KB against an
# audio-dead boot is the media_tuna_v1 trade (HANDOFF lesson 8), not the bm5a* one.
